title: Hitting things with a vehicle
summary: Impacts in R.E.P.O. are measured rather than assumed: a vehicle carries three hurt colliders, impacts are graded small, medium and big from a threshold and a required distance, each grade costs durability of its own, and each shakes the camera and throws particles of its own size.
body: Driving into something is not a single event. A vehicle is built to detect a collision, decide how big it was and then pay for it, which is why a light nudge and a full-speed crash do different things.
It has three hurt colliders. There is a small, a medium and a big one, so what the vehicle can hit is set up in sizes rather than as one shape.

It watches for impacts over a window. There is a detection window, a cooldown after an impact and a further cooldown for each kind, which is why a scrape cannot be counted as a dozen separate crashes.

An impact is graded from a threshold and a distance. Small, medium and big impacts each have a threshold to cross and a distance the object has to be away for that grade, so brushing past and ploughing into something are told apart.

Durability is paid by grade. There is a multiplier for the loss and a separate amount for a small, a medium and a big impact, which is how a vehicle wears out differently depending on how it is driven.
Hitting a monster is handled apart. Each size of impact has its own durability cooldown for enemies, so a run of hits on a creature does not drain the vehicle as fast as the same hits on scenery.

It has a box for enemies and one for bumper cars. There is an enemy impact box transform and a bumper car box, which is why the same vehicle can register a hit on a creature differently from a hit on a fairground car.
The camera takes the hit as well. There are shake strengths for position and rotation with a decay rate, and an intensity for each size of impact, so what you feel matches what you hit.

It also throws sparks of the right size. Each grade has its own impact particles, and there are transforms for the midpoint of the vehicle and for the point of impact, so the effect happens where the collision did rather than at the middle of the model.

What this entry does not tell you: how much durability a vehicle has, how much each grade costs, or how hard you must hit to reach the biggest one. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A vehicle carries a small, a medium and a big hurt collider.
Impacts are detected over a window, with a cooldown and a cooldown per kind.
Small, medium and big impacts each have a threshold and a required distance.
facts.evidence: identifiers: smallImpactThreshold, mediumImpactThreshold, bigImpactThreshold, smallImpactDistanceRequired, mediumImpactDistanceRequired, bigImpactDistanceRequired

facts.claim: Durability loss is scaled by a multiplier with a separate amount for each size of impact.
Each size of impact has its own durability cooldown for enemies.
There is an enemy impact box transform and a bumper car box.
Impacts shake the camera with position and rotation strengths, a decay rate and an intensity for each size.
facts.evidence: identifiers: impactShakePositionStrength, impactShakeRotationStrength, impactShakeDecayRate, impactShakeSmallIntensity, impactShakeMediumIntensity, impactShakeBigIntensity

facts.claim: Each grade of impact has its own particles, and there are transforms for the midpoint and the impact point.
facts.evidence: identifiers: impactParticlesSmall, impactParticlesMedium, impactParticlesBig, midpointTransform, impactTransform
